newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-MORATTI'S DREAM OF GRANDE INTER MUST WAIT.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-MORATTI'S DREAM OF GRANDE INTER MUST WAIT.

text.p: In his youth, Massimo Moratti witnessed the greatest nights in Internazionale Milan's history at the side of his father and club president Angelo.

Together they watched the great Inter side featuring Italian internationals Alessandro Mazzola and Giacinto Facchetti beat Real Madrid in the 1964 European Cup final, retain the trophy against Benfica in 1965 and lose to Celtic in 1967.
They were the days of the "Grande Inter", when the blue-black stripped Milanese club ruled serie A.

On Wednesday night, at the UEFA Cup final second leg against unpretentious Schalke of Germany, the 52-year-old son saw his first European club final as president since taking over in 1995, 27 years after his late father stood down.

In the end, history was all on the side of the Gelsenkirchen side who won a penalty shoot-out to claim the first European club trophy of their 93-year existence and the last UEFA Cup to be fought over the two-legged final format.
Schalke deserved to win, not because they were a better side but because Inter -- winners of the cup twice in the 1990s -- did not do enough to conquer them at San Siro.
Older Inter fans saw little to remind them of the glory days, other than the capacity crowd.
"Its a good lesson," said Moratti. "Taking a few knocks once in a while does you good. You grow from it."
Moratti has sunk a fortune into Inter since he took over, bringing in a host of stars including Frenchman Youri Djorkaeff, England's Paul Ince and Chilean Ivan Zamorano.
Inter started the season as hot favourites for the title. They end it without a trophy, fighting for second place in the league and a slot in the expanded Champions League.
They have flattered to deceive, winning superbly one day and then losing in abject humiliation the next.
The same team has been capable of thrashing Juventus 3-0 in the quarter-finals of the Italian Cup and then losing 4-3 to Sampdoria at home in the league after leading 3-1.
Penalty shoot-outs, more than great goals, have marked their season in the domestic cup and in Europe.
Inter lost their Italian Cup semifinal to Napoli on penalties and reached the third round of the UEFA Cup only after beating unfancied Austrians Casino Graz in a shootout.
In between they slammed seven past Boavista of Portugal in the UEFA cup and dismissed much-fancied Monaco.
"To win an international trophy against whoever it may be, you need a personality, guided by one or more brains," wrote the editor of the Gazzetta dello Sport on Thursday.
"Inter has a soul, a heart and generosity but its true personality remains a mystery. Nobody leads, nobody thinks."
English coach Roy Hodgson warned last summer that it would be asking too much to expect Inter to win a trophy in what amounted to a season of consolidation.
The trouble for Inter and Moratti is that a club can only have so many seasons of transition.

"I took over Inter when it was almost in serie B and with me every year has been better," Moratti said on Wednesday night. "Of course tonight is a huge disappointment...we lost this cup in Germany. Patience. Things will get better."
Hodgson, whistled and jeered by fans on Wednesday, is leaving for Blackburn in England to be replaced by Luigi Simoni, fired as Napoli coach earlier in the season.
With him will come Brazilians Andre Cruz and Caio. Barcelona's Ronaldo, target of an Inter bid, may or may not while Ince could be the big departure of the summer.
The unsettled Englishman is one player that Moratti would like to hang on to as the midfield fighter and crowd favourite whose stature has grown with every game in Italy.
"I don't know, I really don't know what he will do," said Moratti when asked. "But this match could have been important in convincing him to stay."
